s01.text: Here is a model with seven billion weights, sitting in fourteen gigabytes of memory.

s02.text: Now make it write a long document. Every token it writes gets stored.

s03.text: Not just the token. The key and the value vector, for every layer, for every head.

s04.text: That is the key-value cache. It is the reason long context is expensive.

s05.text: The arithmetic for one token: thirty-two layers, each keeping a key and a value for every head.

s06.text: That is about half a megabyte per token, in half precision, for a model this size.

s07.text: A hundred thousand tokens of context is fifty gigabytes. For one conversation.

s08.text: The model itself is fourteen gigabytes. The cache is now the bigger number.

s09.text: Which flips the question. It is not how big is the model. It is how much are you going to ask it.

s10.text: You can shrink the cache. Compress it, evict it, quantise it, or share the heads.

s11.text: Every one of those is a trade. Compression costs accuracy, eviction costs context.

s12.text: And none of them is free. They are all the same move: fit more context into less memory.

s13.text: The model is the thing you trained. The cache is the thing you pay for.
